Calculate the living population at time points

Source: R/calculate_population_size.R
calculate_population_size.Rd

Calculate population counts from a returned simulation result or a starting population, at chosen time points. Counts can be disaggregated by stratifying variables.

Usage

calculate_population_size(
  population,
  times,
  by = NULL,
  use_detailed_previous_union = TRUE
)

Arguments

population

A hammel_population object either returned from run_simulation() or built as a baseline starting population.

times

A numeric vector of finite time points in years at which to calculate population size.

by

Character vector of variables to disaggregate population counts by. Defaults to NULL for no disaggregation. Populations counts can be disaggregated by "sex", "union_type", "previous_union" and any declared group dimensions.

use_detailed_previous_union

Logical value that indicates whether disaggregation by "previous_union" will use "separated" and "widowed" or a combined "dissolved" category.

Value

A tibble with time, the by columns and population.

Details

The by argument can take the standard variables of sex, union_type, or previous_union as well as any group variables defined in the population input.

The user can input any numeric value for times (including decimal values), but no value may come after the end_time of the simulation.

Examples

# calculate population size on a generatd population
pop_start <- generate_uniform_population(1000, end_time = 0)
calculate_population_size(pop_start, times = c(-10, -5, 0))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>    time population
#>   <dbl>      <int>
#> 1   -10        861
#> 2    -5        934
#> 3     0       1000

# run a simulation
model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_population(pop_start) |>
  set_fertility(usa_2000_fertility) |>
  set_mortality(usa_2000_mortality) |>
  set_union_formation("on_demand")
pop_end <- run_simulation(model, 100)

# calculate at 20 year intervals
calculate_population_size(pop_end, times = seq(0, 100, 20))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 2
#>    time population
#>   <dbl>      <int>
#> 1     0       1000
#> 2    20       1100
#> 3    40       1146
#> 4    60       1165
#> 5    80       1245
#> 6   100       1313

# caclulate at 20 year intervals by sex
calculate_population_size(pop_end, times = seq(0, 100, 20), by = "sex")
#> # A tibble: 12 × 3
#>     time sex   population
#>    <dbl> <chr>      <int>
#>  1     0 m            491
#>  2    20 m            511
#>  3    40 m            524
#>  4    60 m            524
#>  5    80 m            580
#>  6   100 m            612
#>  7     0 f            509
#>  8    20 f            589
#>  9    40 f            622
#> 10    60 f            641
#> 11    80 f            665
#> 12   100 f            701
